steps.a: There are 64 characterization tests, good. I considered an enum with an abstract method per constant, but several methods need injected collaborators (the FX rate service for WALLET, the merchant tier repo for CARD), which enums can't take cleanly. I'll use a FeeStrategy interface with one Spring bean per method, collected into an EnumMap keyed by the method each bean declares.
Created SepaFee, AchFee, WalletFee and BnplFee the same way, moving each case body verbatim.

steps.a: Refactor done: each payment method's fee rule is now its own FeeStrategy bean, and FeeCalculator only dispatches through an EnumMap, failing at startup on duplicates and at call time on unknown methods. All 64 existing fee tests pass unchanged and the full build is green (1,288 tests).

reference.summary: Replaced a 300-line switch in a payments fee calculator with the strategy pattern: one Spring-managed strategy per payment method, dispatched through an enum map that rejects duplicates at startup. Behaviour was preserved, with all 64 existing fee tests and the full suite passing.
facts: The calculator had a long switch over payment methods
Each case body moved into its own FeeStrategy implementation registered as a Spring bean
The calculator builds an EnumMap and throws on duplicate or unknown methods
All 64 fee tests and the full build of 1,288 tests pass
specific: replacing a switch statement with polymorphism

decisions.choice: Use a strategy interface with Spring beans instead of an enum with per-constant methods
decisions.reason: some strategies need injected collaborators that enums cannot take cleanly
